How to use

Who it's for

Massage blends

Long used in body oils for its warmth, and gentle enough to use at an ordinary dilution.

Anyone who finds oregano too harsh

The same family, far softer — warm rather than medicinal.

Simple evening diffusing

Pairs naturally with lavender and needs no skill to blend.

What people get wrong

Confusing it with oregano. They are close relatives, but oregano is far higher in carvacrol, much harsher on skin, and needs a lower dilution. The names are sometimes used loosely by suppliers.

Using it in pregnancy. Marjoram appears on most avoid lists, and its mildness makes people assume otherwise.

What it won't do

Sweet marjoram and Spanish marjoram are different plants — the latter is a thyme species. Check the botanical name if you have bought marjoram before.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Sweet Marjoram

Is marjoram the same as oregano?

They are related and sometimes confused, including by suppliers. Sweet marjoram is Origanum majorana, soft and warm. Oregano is Origanum vulgare, much sharper and a far stronger skin irritant.

Can I use it in cooking?

No. None of our oils are food grade or sold for internal use. Use the dried or fresh herb.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. Avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.
